what: The observations the P1-27 lifecycle turns on, and the state this repository declares as a result. scripts/ci/check-p1-27-lifecycle.mjs derives the same state from the tree and fails if the two disagree.
why: The phase carried a closure rule that could not be satisfied in any order: the branch may not merge until every task row is PASS, a row may not be PASS while its reproof is OUTSTANDING, and the reproof is a job only the merge starts. The cycle came from writing two different facts into one word. They are separated now — FINAL_VERDICT is the TASK verdict, PROTECTED_REPROOF_STATUS is a lifecycle property — and this file is where the lifecycle facts live.
authority: docs/phase-1/phase-1-27/canonical-plan.md states P1-27-QA-005 in full as "Regression and immutable evidence packaging" and binds no canonical task to protected develop. The plan mentions protected change control exactly twice and both mentions route a BACKEND defect through protected remediation. So QA-005 is CANDIDATE ASSURANCE and may PASS before the merge once the exact-head evidence is complete, and a protected re-run is a property of the gate lifecycle rather than a requirement of any task.
whatThisIsNot: This is a RECORD of observations, not the observations. A cell claiming GREEN or RED must name a run id, a job id and a 40-hex head; the gate refuses a claim carrying none of those, and refuses a head that is not the code candidate. It cannot make a false but well-formed record true, and nothing here should be read as though it could.

observations.CODE_CANDIDATE_NOTE: NOT FROZEN AT THIS HEAD, and that is the honest value. This branch changes executable files, so any run taken before it would describe a different tree. The candidate is the CODE candidate rather than the head commit on purpose: recording the result of a run changes the tree, so a literal exact-head rule is stale the moment it is satisfied. Documentation-only commits after the freeze do not supersede it, and executableChangesSince proves that by asking git which paths moved and classifying each with classify-changes.mjs, the repository's own authority for what documentation is. The previous code candidate, 03e84f1f244252903569619de72481f30238e76a, was superseded by exactly this rule: six committed executable files changed after it, so its hosted CI, CodeQL, web artefact and authenticated-browser runs are HISTORICAL ONLY and are cited nowhere as evidence about the current tree.

CANDIDATE_HOSTED_CI.note: No hosted run has been taken against the current tree. The last exact-head hosted run recorded by this phase, run 31312531302 at head 356f1a1e937e819b9db94f40a2d6f04f98f9ae39, is recorded in ci-evidence.md as SUPERSEDED and is not evidence about this tree.

CANDIDATE_AUTHENTICATED_BROWSER.note: The tier is wired, governed and called by both gates: pr-ci.yml on every pull request whose head is a branch of this repository, and protected-develop-verification.yml on a protected push. It has executed three times in this repository's history — runs 31337158296, 31343632011 and 31347643485, all recorded run by run in .github/ci-baselines/unrun-test-tiers.json — and all three predate the closing wave. None is an observation of this tree. This is the condition 23 task rows carry as PENDING_CANDIDATE_OBSERVATION, and it is discharged by a PULL-REQUEST run rather than by the merge, which is why it belongs here and not under a protected-only heading.

PROTECTED_MERGE.note: A protected merge is verified by its SECOND parent. The first parent of a merge commit on develop is develop, so checking the first parent proves only that develop is develop.

PROTECTED_CI.note: Not reachable before the merge. protected-develop-verification.yml runs on pushes to develop and main and by workflow_dispatch.

PROTECTED_AUTHENTICATED_BROWSER.note: The same tier as above, taken again from the protected caller. It is a re-run of a proof already taken at the candidate, not a different proof, and nothing at the candidate is held hostage to it.

PROTECTED_ONLY_OBLIGATIONS.why: A CodeQL pull-request run is diff-informed and says so in its own output, so it cannot establish the repository-wide ceiling. Only an analysis of a protected ref can. This is a phase-level lifecycle obligation and it is deliberately NOT attached to any task row: no canonical task's requirement is proved or disproved by it.
protected-gate runs only on a push to a protected branch. Nothing before the merge can produce its verdict.

OWNER_ACCEPTANCE.note: The Owner returned OWNER ACCEPTANCE: FAIL on 2026-08-06 against a merged application, and the phase was reopened. That verdict is history and is recorded in owner-acceptance-fail-remediation.md; it is not a standing verdict about this candidate, which the Owner has not seen. `result` is null because acceptance is the Owner's act against the running application, it is not derivable from any count in this repository, and silence is not Pass.

declared.note: Every blocker here is an expected state of an unfinished phase, not a fault. The gate fails when this declaration and the tree disagree in EITHER direction: a new blocker that is not declared, and a declared blocker the tree no longer raises. That is what makes it a check rather than a printout.
